note: SPEC-V2-2223. One entry per WCAG 2.2 A and AA success criterion. static names the rows that check it statically (pack:row). taught_by names catalog rows that teach it without checking. runtime names the axe-core rules a rendered audit runs for it. manual says what only a person can judge. teach is the rule as a builder applies it.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.teach: Every carries alt: web-launch checks the built HTML, and Svelte's a11y_missing_attribute checks the source. A decorative image takes alt="". An icon-only control gets its name under 4.1.2. A card image that shows words carries those words in its alt. Whether an alt text serves the same purpose as the image is a person's judgement.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.manual: whether a transcript or an audio track is equivalent to prerecorded audio-only or video-only media is judged by a person
criteria.teach: A prerecorded audio-only clip, such as a pronunciation clip, ships a text alternative. A video-only clip ships a text alternative or an audio track. A clip that only repeats text already on the screen, and is labelled as such, is exempt.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.teach: A <video> with sound carries <track kind="captions">. Subtitles are not captions, because captions also carry speaker changes and sounds. A muted decorative loop owes no captions.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.manual: whether an audio description or a media alternative covers what the video shows needs a person
criteria.teach: A prerecorded video with sound carries an audio description, or a full text alternative (a transcript that also describes what is shown). Link the alternative beside the player.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.manual: live media is out of a static read's reach; a live stream needs live captions from a person or a service
criteria.teach: Any live audio in synchronized media, such as a live lesson, is captioned live. DeckStreak ships no live media, and this pack records the rule for when it does.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.manual: whether audio description covers the visual information needs a person
criteria.teach: A prerecorded video carries audio description: <track kind="descriptions">, a described version, or narration that already says what is shown.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.teach: Structure is in the markup, not only in the look: headings are <h1>-<h6> in order, lists are lists, tables have <th>, fields have labels, and a group of radios sits in a <fieldset> with a <legend>. aria-hidden never hides focusable content.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.manual: whether the reading order a screen reader follows keeps the meaning needs a person, and CSS order, flex-direction: *-reverse and grid placement can change it
criteria.teach: The DOM order is the reading order. Reorder visually only where the meaning does not depend on the sequence, and never reorder a card's question and answer.

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.manual: instructions are copy, and whether they rely only on shape, colour, size, position or sound is read by a person
criteria.teach: Instructions name the control, not only where it is or how it looks: "press Flip", not "press the round button on the right".

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.teach: Content works in portrait and landscape. Telegram's lockOrientation(), screen.orientation.lock() and a manifest orientation lock all fail unless an orientation is essential (a piano keyboard, a bank cheque). Record that with an a11y-exception: comment that gives the reason.

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.teach: A field that collects the user's own data (name, email, tel, one-time-code) names its purpose with an autocomplete token from HTML's list.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.manual: whether colour is the only cue is judged on the rendered page
criteria.teach: Colour is never the only cue. A correct or wrong answer shows an icon and a word as well as green or red. Links in body text are underlined, or differ by 3:1 and gain a non-colour cue on hover and focus.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.teach: Audio that plays on its own for more than three seconds can be paused or stopped, or its volume set apart from the system's. Pronunciation clips play only on request.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.teach: Text contrasts 4.5:1, and large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold) 3:1. contrast-pairs computes the ratio wherever one rule sets both colours statically. web-launch's contrast row checks a declared data-contrast marker. The runtime audit measures the rendered pairs, including Telegram's --tg-theme-* colours, which only exist at runtime.

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.teach: Text resizes to 200% without loss. Never set user-scalable=no or a maximum-scale under 2, size text in rem, and let containers grow with their text.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.manual: whether an image holds text that could have been text needs a person
criteria.teach: Use real text, not pictures of text. A logotype is the exception. A card that shows a word shows it as text, so it can be resized, recoloured and read aloud.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.teach: Content reflows at 320 CSS px wide without scrolling in two dimensions. Telegram's webview on a small phone is exactly this case.

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.manual: component boundaries, states and focus rings against their adjacent colours need the rendered page
criteria.teach: The visual parts that identify a control, its state and meaningful graphics contrast 3:1 with what is next to them: input borders, the checked state and chart lines.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.teach: Nothing breaks when the user sets line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2, letter-spacing 0.12 and word-spacing 0.16 times the font size. Never lock them inline with !important, and avoid fixed-height text boxes.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.teach: Content shown on hover or focus can be dismissed with Escape, can itself be hovered, and stays until dismissed. A hover-only reveal also fails the keyboard, so give every :hover reveal a :focus-within twin.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.teach: Everything works from a keyboard. Use <button> and <a href>. A custom widget takes tabindex="0", a role and Enter and Space handlers, which is failure F54's remedy.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.manual: a keyboard trap is found by tabbing through the rendered page
criteria.teach: Focus can always leave a component. A modal holds focus on purpose and releases it on Escape and on close, and a third-party widget is tested for traps.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.teach: A single-character shortcut (j for next, f for flip) can be turned off or remapped, or works only while its control has focus. Otherwise require a modifier.

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.teach: Every time limit can be turned off, adjusted to ten times, or extended with 20 seconds' warning. The exceptions are real-time events, an essential limit and limits over 20 hours. A timed drill offers the choice before it starts, and a delayed <meta http-equiv="refresh"> is never used.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.teach: Moving, blinking or auto-updating content that starts itself and lasts over five seconds can be paused, stopped or hidden. Celebrations end on their own, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.manual: whether an animation flashes (a luminance or red change) needs the rendered frames, for example through PEAT
criteria.teach: Nothing flashes more than three times in any second. Keep confetti, chest openings and streak bursts under three cycles a second, or below the general and red flash thresholds.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.teach: Repeated blocks can be skipped: a skip link, or landmarks (<main>, <nav>) that assistive technology jumps between.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.teach: Every page has a title that names its topic. A SvelteKit single-page app sets <title> per route in <svelte:head>, because the static shell's title never changes.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.teach: Focus moves in an order that keeps the meaning. No tabindex above 0, and a dialog moves focus in on open and back to its opener on close.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.teach: A link's purpose is clear from its text, or from its text and its context. "Review Spanish deck", not "click here".

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.manual: more than one way to reach a page is a site-structure judgement, and a Mini App's screens that are steps of one process are exempt
criteria.teach: A set of pages offers two ways to find a page: navigation plus search, a site map or a table of contents.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.manual: whether a heading or a label describes its topic or purpose is read by a person
criteria.teach: Headings and labels say what follows. Svelte's a11y_missing_content catches the empty ones.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.teach: Keyboard focus is always visible. Never outline: none without a :focus-visible replacement.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.teach: A focused control is never entirely hidden by author content. A sticky header or bottom bar, such as the Mini App's main button bar, pairs with scroll-padding (technique C43), so a scrolled-to control clears it.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.teach: A multipoint or path-based gesture (a swipe to grade, a pinch to zoom) has a single-pointer alternative, such as a button.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.teach: Act on the up event, not on the down event, so a mistaken press can be dragged away and aborted (failure F101).

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.teach: A control's accessible name contains its visible label, best at the start, so a speech user can say what they see (failure F96).

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.teach: Anything triggered by shaking or tilting (Telegram's Accelerometer, DeviceOrientation and Gyroscope; devicemotion) also has a control, and the motion response can be turned off.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.teach: Every drag (reorder cards, slide to answer) has a single-pointer alternative without dragging.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.teach: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or are spaced so that a 24 px circle around each touches no other. ux-laws teaches 44 px as the comfortable size.

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.teach: <html lang> names the page's language. With Paraglide, app.html's lang follows the locale, so the value changes when the learner switches language.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.teach: Every passage in another language carries lang. cjk-typography checks CJK passages and the script subtags zh-Hans and zh-Hant. A French or Spanish example inside English copy is the author's to tag, as <span lang="fr">.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.teach: Receiving focus never navigates, submits or moves focus away (failure F55).

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.teach: Changing a control's value never navigates or submits, unless the user was told first. A <select> of decks changes a view in place, and a button opens the deck (failures F36 and F37).

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.manual: the same relative order of navigation across pages is a comparison of rendered pages
criteria.teach: Navigation repeated across pages keeps its order. Keep it in one shared +layout.svelte.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.manual: whether the same function is identified the same way everywhere is a person's comparison
criteria.teach: A function with the same purpose has the same name and icon on every screen (for example "Flip", never "Turn" elsewhere).

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.manual: the relative position of help across pages is a comparison of rendered pages
criteria.teach: Help (the bot's /help, a contact link or self-help) sits in the same place relative to the page on every screen. Put it in the shared layout.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.teach: A detected input error names the field and says what is wrong, in text. Set aria-invalid and point aria-describedby at the message.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.teach: Every field has a label, and every format constraint has an instruction next to it.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.manual: whether a known correction is suggested needs a person to read the messages
criteria.teach: When a correction is known, suggest it ("Did you mean 私?"), unless doing so defeats the purpose, as in a quiz answer.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.manual: which actions spend, delete or commit, and whether each is reversible, checked or confirmed, is a design review
criteria.teach: Spending coins, buying a streak repair, deleting a deck and erasing an account are each reversible, checked, or confirmed before they take effect.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.manual: whether a process asks again for what it already has needs a walk through the process
criteria.teach: Within one process, never ask again for what the user already entered. Auto-fill it or offer it to select.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.teach: No step of logging in needs a cognitive test unless there is an alternative or a mechanism: let password managers fill fields (never autocomplete="off") and allow paste. Telegram's initData login needs no test at all.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.teach: Every control's name and role can be determined, and its state is exposed. Use native elements first. A custom one takes a valid WAI-ARIA role and the states its role requires, and ids that ARIA references are unique.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.teach: A status message (a toast saying the card was saved, a streak update) is announced without taking focus: role="status" or aria-live="polite", and role="alert" for errors.

removed.name: Parsing
removed.note: obsolete and removed in WCAG 2.2; web-launch's duplicate-ids row is kept under 4.1.2, for ids that ARIA references

out_of_scope.note: the target is AA; ux-laws teaches 2.5.5's 44 px as the comfortable target, and ui-styles teaches 2.4.13's focus appearance
